findings.description: The requested story should follow a feature request into a user story and acceptance criteria, but the opening starts at an already written story ('Say a team writes: As a learner ...'), so the request-to-story step is missing. Smallest fix, no net word growth: open the story with the request, e.g. 'Learners ask to save unfinished notes. The team writes: ...' and drop 'Say a team writes:'. Keep the step at or under 120 words (now 99).

Step-1 coherence: under the heading 'Start with a guess', the AI and user-story framing is followed directly by an unrelated sprint scenario ('A team works in two-week sprints...') and the end-of-sprint prediction, with no bridge. A second, different 'team' also appears. A learner may read the prediction as being about the draft-note story. Add a short bridge in the sprint sentence, for example 'First, how does that team plan its work? It works in two-week sprints...', or reuse 'the team', so the switch to the sprint guess is clear. The opening does not give away the step-1 prediction (no Review or Retrospective is mentioned) or the step-4 testable-criterion choice. It previews the As a / I want / so that form before step 3 teaches it, which is acceptable as a worked example because step 3 teaches the form again before the card check.

New item 'o3 - Story defines success': distractor D 'Most criteria passing, since one of two is close enough' contains a self-undermining cue ('close enough') that removes it without recall. The keyed option also nearly restates the page's bold sentence, so the item leans toward recognition. Rewrite D as a belief a learner could really hold, e.g. 'The header row, since it is the first criterion you can see', with matching feedback. Keep the key at C. Everything else passes: one correct answer, feedback on every option, ASCII only, colons escaped (AC1\:, AC2\:), no length cue (options are 58-63 characters), existing three items unchanged, and keys D/B/A/C balance A-D.
